---
title: "8. Subsetting, integration, differential expression, and pseudobulk"
---

## Why subset and recluster?

In a whole tumor microenvironment, early PCs may separate immune from stromal cells, or myeloid from lymphoid cells. Those axes can overwhelm subtle T-cell differences.

After subsetting T cells, rerun feature selection, scaling, PCA, neighbors, clustering, and UMAP so the reference frame is defined by T-cell variation.

```r
tcells <- subset(obj, subset = truth_cell_type %in% c("CD4_T", "CD8_T"))
tcells <- NormalizeData(tcells)
tcells <- FindVariableFeatures(tcells)
tcells <- ScaleData(tcells)
tcells <- RunPCA(tcells)
tcells <- FindNeighbors(tcells, dims = 1:20)
tcells <- FindClusters(tcells, resolution = 0.6)
tcells <- RunUMAP(tcells, dims = 1:20)
```

## Integration/batch correction

Integration methods attempt to reduce unwanted technical structure while preserving biology. The key question is not "did batches mix?" but **did we remove unwanted technical effects without erasing condition/tissue biology?**

No algorithm can rescue a perfectly confounded design. If all controls were processed on Day 1 and all disease samples on Day 2, batch and biology cannot be uniquely separated computationally.

## Differential expression

`FindMarkers()` can compare predefined groups, but when making donor-level claims you must respect biological replication.

Suppose six donors contribute thousands of T cells. For a treatment comparison, `n` is typically six donors, not the total number of cells.

## Pseudobulk logic

Aggregate raw counts within each biological replicate and cell population, then use bulk RNA-seq frameworks such as edgeR/DESeq2/limma-voom.

Conceptually:

$$
\text{Donor A CD8 pseudobulk}_g
= \sum_{c \in \text{Donor A CD8 cells}} x_{g,c}
$$

Pseudobulk asks whether **replicate-level** expression differs between conditions while preserving the biological unit of replication.

## Composition is a separate question

A treatment can change the proportion of CD8 T cells without changing expression within CD8 cells, or vice versa. Cell abundance/composition analysis and within-cell-type differential expression should be treated as distinct analyses.
